reason: The text extensively portrays the Hebrews/Israelites as followers of the God Yahweh (יְהוָה). Throughout the narrative, Yahweh communicates directly with Moses and Aaron, performs miracles on behalf of the Hebrews (the plagues, the parting of the Red Sea, providing manna and water), and the Hebrews are repeatedly shown worshiping Yahweh, following His commandments, and trusting in His protection. Key passages include: the establishment of the Passover as a statute to Yahweh, the Hebrews' belief in Yahweh after witnessing His deliverance ('וַיַּֽאֲמִ֙ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה'), God's leading them with pillar of cloud and fire, and the consistent framing of the exodus as Yahweh's salvation of His people. Even during moments of complaint, the narrative structure assumes Yahweh as the people's God and protector.
